patients.summary: Former construction laborer on disability with severe alcohol use disorder who joins in 2021 with hypertension and peptic ulcer disease, is found to have alcoholic cirrhosis in 2023, and decompensates with ascites, encephalopathy and variceal bleeding through 2026, ending with a TIPS and an open transplant evaluation.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife phoned on his behalf. Their old PCP office stopped taking his plan and he has been out of refills twice this year. Medicaid card info taken, eligibility verified with the plan. Booked new patient appt next week, 40 min slot. Asked that he bring all pill bottles and the name of the old office so we can request records. Release form emailed to the address on file.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

50 y/o man here to establish. Previous PCP office no longer took his insurance; he has been stretching his BP pills. Wife waited in the car.

HTN: told he had high pressure around 2016, on amlodipine 5 since. Does not check at home. No headaches, chest pain, dyspnea.

Ulcer history: had an ulcer around 2017 at the old office, treated, has stayed on pantoprazole daily since. No current heartburn, no black stools, no vomiting.

Alcohol: drinks beer every day, usually a six-pack, has for about 13 years, more on weekends. Has had stretches of cutting back that do not last. No withdrawal seizures or DTs he knows of. Has never been in a program. Not interested in a referral today, said he would try to cut down on his own.

Tobacco: about two-thirds of a pack a day since his early twenties. Tried quitting once with gum.

Work: laborer on building crews for most of his life; out on disability leave now.

Family: father drank heavily and died of liver cirrhosis at 58. Mother has hypertension and type 2 diabetes. A brother also struggles with alcohol.

Meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, pantoprazole 40 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: BP 142/90 seated, repeated similar. Well appearing, a little ruddy. Sclerae white. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass felt, no distension. No edema. Gait steady.

AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-2 1.

A/P
1. Hypertension, above goal on amlodipine 5. Away from meds on and off; refilled, recheck in a few months before changing anything.
2. Peptic ulcer disease, history - continue pantoprazole.
3. Alcohol use disorder, severe by history. Talked plainly about his dad's liver and what daily use does. He wants to try cutting down first. Gave the program list; door is open.
4. Tobacco - advised to quit, he will think about it; offered patch or other aids.
5. Health maintenance - Tdap today. Fasting labs ordered. Records request for old practice. Colon screening: says he did a stool card last year, will confirm with records.

Return 3-4 months.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 14 pages, covering 2015-2021 (original visit dates 2015-03 through 2021-02).

Problem list on their summary: Hypertension (since 2016). Peptic ulcer disease (2017), treated, on maintenance PPI. Tobacco use. Alcohol use.
Medications: amlodipine 5 mg daily; pantoprazole 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Screening: FIT 2020-06, negative.
Last visit 2021-02: BP 146/92, counseled on alcohol and smoking, refills given.

Scanned to chart under outside records. Reviewed by PCP.

documents.title: Lab reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Scott, a reminder that the bloodwork ordered at your first visit has not been drawn yet. You can walk in to the lab any weekday morning; nothing to eat after midnight the night before. Reply here if you need the order resent.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu vaccine. Per PCP standing order also given PCV20 (smoker, daily alcohol use). Flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, PCV20 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Tolerated well, waited 15 min. FIT kit handed to pt with instructions since his last one was 2020. Reminded about fasting labs; he says he will go next week.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in a year. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u HTN.

Taking amlodipine every day now that he has refills on auto-fill. No side effects, no ankle swelling. Still drinking most days, "maybe a little less" - roughly 5-6 cans. Still smoking. Labs from August never drawn, he keeps meaning to.

BP 138/88. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
- HTN: closer. Stay on amlodipine 5. Recheck at physical.
- Alcohol/tobacco: not ready for treatment; brief counseling again. He knows the number to call.
- Labs: order still active; MA walked him to the scheduling desk to book a draw before his physical.

Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

52 y/o man for yearly exam; rescheduled from last month. Fasting labs drawn this AM, finally.

Interval: no ER visits. BP meds daily. Beer most days, about six. Smoking 2/3 ppd, figures 20 pack-years give or take. Sleeping ok. Mood fine, PHQ-9 3. Wife is after him to cut back.

ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no abdominal pain, no blood in stool, no vomiting blood, no swelling.

Meds: amlodipine 5 daily, pantoprazole 40 daily. NKDA.

Exam: BP 138/88. Alert, conversant. Eyes anicteric. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organ enlargement appreciated, no fluid. Skin without rash. No edema. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
- Preventive: flu and first Shingrix today. Lung screening CT ordered - meets criteria with his pack-years. FIT due next month; kit at front desk.
- HCV and HIV screening sent with today's labs.
- HTN: acceptable, continue amlodipine.
- Alcohol: same conversation, same answer. Will look at the liver tests with him.
- Tobacco: advised to stop.

See results note.

documents.title: Physical lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Scott - your labs are back. Kidney function, sugar and cholesterol are fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV tests are negative. Two things stand out: your liver enzymes are up (AST 76, ALT 52) and your platelet count is a little low at 138. That pattern fits with daily drinking stressing the liver. The best treatment is cutting way back or stopping. I would like to repeat these in about 3 months - the lab order is in. If you want help with the drinking, the program list I gave you still stands, or call me.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (BASELINE)
Indication: 52-year-old current smoker, approximately 20 pack-years.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: Lungs are clear without nodule, mass or consolidation. No emphysema. Airways patent. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No acute osseous abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung screening CT clear, Lung-RADS 1. Repeat in one year. Still the best thing for these lungs is quitting. Released to portal.
